report.incidentSummary: Starting around 10:05 IST (04:35 UTC) on 2026-10-09, users asking the AI assistant about their portfolio received responses stating they held no funds, despite the Portfolio UI screen showing holdings normally. Following a push notification sent to 2.1M users at 04:30 UTC, user-context-service experienced worker pool saturation and timeout spikes fetching holdings between 04:35 and 05:15 UTC. On timeout, user-context-service executed a fallback handler that cached empty holdings ('holdings=0 sips=0') into shared cache with an excessively long TTL of 21600 seconds (6 hours). While timeout counts returned to baseline at 05:15 UTC, the poisoned cache entries caused the assistant to continue serving empty context to affected users through noon IST.
report.rootCauseStatement: During a morning timeout burst between 04:35 and 05:15 UTC, user-context-service fell back to writing an empty portfolio context ('holdings=0 sips=0') to the shared cache with a 6-hour (21600s) TTL instead of failing open or caching with a minimal transient TTL. This poisoned the cache for affected users, causing assistant-orchestrator to retrieve and present zero holdings long after upstream request timeouts returned to baseline.

hypotheses.cause: user-context-service wrote fallback empty context entries ('holdings=0 sips=0') with an excessive 6-hour TTL (21600s) into shared cache when holdings fetches timed out, poisoning the cache and serving zero holdings through noon.
hypotheses.rationale: Logs from user-context-service explicitly demonstrate 254 timeout errors between 04:35 and 05:15 UTC triggering fallback cache writes of 'holdings=0 sips=0' with ttl=21600s. Cache hit rates for the user_context keyspace rose from 93% to 98%, and user-context-service served 390 empty context reads from cache between 05:15 and 07:30 UTC, directly explaining the persistent noon symptom.

hypotheses.cause: A push notification campaign sent to 2.1M users at 04:30 UTC saturated user-context-service worker pools, causing requests to queue and time out.
hypotheses.rationale: The notification campaign scheduled at 04:30 UTC correlates with the onset of worker pool congestion at 04:35 UTC. However, capacity saturation alone cannot explain why symptoms persisted through 07:30 UTC (noon IST), as worker pool timeouts fully subsided at 05:15 UTC.

hypotheses.cause: Deployment of portfolio-service v7.2.1 at 04:28 UTC broke pagination or response contracts for user-context-service, causing failed or stalled holdings fetches.
hypotheses.rationale: portfolio-service latency remained completely stable at 135-153ms p95 across the entire window, and timeouts in user-context-service dropped back to near-zero after 05:15 UTC without any rollback or fix to portfolio-service.

facts.statement: At 04:28 UTC (09:58 IST), notification-service scheduled campaign CHG-48220 ('Ask the assistant about your SIPs') pushing to 2.1M users at 04:30 UTC, and portfolio-service deployed version 7.2.1 under CHG-48227.
user-context-service timeout_count surged from 0 to 48.84 count/min and error_rate spiked from 0.3% to 12.3% starting at 04:35 UTC, subsiding back to baseline by 05:15 UTC.
user-context-service logged 254 instances of 'context build timed out after #ms (holdings fetch pending); worker pool #/# busy, # queued' between 04:35:01Z and 05:14:50Z.
When context builds timed out, user-context-service executed fallback cache writes: 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'.

After timeouts normalized at 05:15 UTC, missing_context_rate remained elevated between 8.5% and 9.8% through 07:25 UTC, and user-context-service logged 390 instances of serving empty context from cache.
portfolio-service p95 latency remained steady at 134-153 ms throughout 04:00 to 07:30 UTC.
Cache hit rate for the user_context keyspace rose from 93.2% prior to 04:35 UTC to 97.6% by 04:55 UTC and stayed around 97-98% through 07:25 UTC, while cache memory and evictions remained normal.

inferences.statement: The push notification campaign CHG-48220 triggered a sudden surge in chat traffic around 04:30-04:35 UTC, saturating user-context-service's worker pool and causing holdings fetch calls to time out.

Caching 'holdings=0 sips=0' with a 6-hour TTL during upstream timeouts poisoned the cache for affected users, directly causing assistant-orchestrator to report zero holdings through noon IST even after worker pool congestion cleared.

portfolio-service v7.2.1 deployment was not the cause of holdings retrieval failure because portfolio-service latency remained normal and timeouts naturally subsided at 05:15 UTC without deployment changes.

assumptions.statement: assistant-orchestrator relies strictly on user-context-service context payloads to determine whether a user holds funds, without querying portfolio-service directly.

timeline.event: portfolio-service deployed version 7.2.1 (CHG-48227) and notification campaign CHG-48220 was configured.
Notification campaign 'Ask the assistant about your SIPs' broadcasted to 2.1M users.
user-context-service worker pool saturated; timeouts surged to ~32-49 count/min and error rate rose to ~12%.
user-context-service began executing fallback cache writes storing 'holdings=0 sips=0' with ttl=21600s (6 hours).
missing_context_rate peaked at 23.24% on user-context-service.
Timeouts and error rates returned to baseline (~0 count/min, ~0.3%), but user-context-service began serving cached empty contexts (390 occurrences logged).
Support lead reported incident INC-6376 as users continued receiving empty portfolio responses at noon.

confidence.rationale: Application logs from user-context-service explicitly prove that timeouts caused empty context writes with ttl=21600s, and metric telemetry confirms elevated cache hit rates and persistent 9% missing_context_rate lasting past 07:25 UTC.

gaps.description: Specific user-level cache key inspection at noon IST was not performed via tools.
gaps.impact: Minimal; aggregate logs and metrics provide clear proof of 21600s TTL cache writes and subsequent empty cache reads.

recommendedActions.action: Flush or invalidate poisoned user_context keys in shared cache matching pattern 'user_ctx:u_*' where holdings=0 and sips=0 created between 04:35 and 05:15 UTC.
recommendedActions.rationale: Removes the 6-hour poisoned cache entries immediately so user-context-service fetches fresh holdings from portfolio-service.
recommendedActions.verification: Query user-context-service missing_context_rate and confirm it drops from ~9% back to baseline <1%, and verify test assistant queries reflect actual holdings.

recommendedActions.action: Modify user-context-service fallback error handling to avoid caching empty context on timeout, or set a short negative TTL (e.g., 30-60 seconds) rather than 21600 seconds.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents transient downstream latency or worker pool saturation from poisoning user context for 6 hours.
recommendedActions.verification: Review code diff and verify in staging that simulated portfolio-service timeouts do not write ttl=21600s empty entries to cache.

recommendedActions.action: Implement concurrency rate limiting or scale worker pools in user-context-service ahead of large notification push campaigns.
recommendedActions.rationale: Ensures sudden surges in assistant conversation turns driven by marketing campaigns do not exhaust context worker pools.
recommendedActions.verification: Conduct load tests matching notification push volumes (2M+ users) and verify timeout_count remains at zero.

incident.summary: Since around 10:00 IST many users asking the assistant about their portfolio get "you don't hold any funds" even though the Portfolio screen shows their holdings. Still happening for a lot of users at noon.

incident.userImpact: Wrong personal answers from the assistant; users worry their investments are gone.

candidates.whyPlausible: The Portfolio screen queries portfolio-service directly via api-gateway and functions normally, whereas the assistant relies specifically on user-context-service to fetch and assemble portfolio context. candidates.wouldConfirm: A deployment of user-context-service just prior to 04:35 UTC accompanied by an increase in missing_context_rate, error_rate, or logs showing empty context returned despite valid portfolio data.

candidates.whyPlausible: user-context-service has a tight 1000ms timeout with zero retries when calling portfolio-service. ## Summary
Starting around 10:05 IST (04:35 UTC) on 2026-10-09, users asking the AI assistant about their portfolio received responses stating they held no funds, despite the Portfolio UI screen showing holdings normally. Following a push notification sent to 2.1M users at 04:30 UTC, user-context-service experienced worker pool saturation and timeout spikes fetching holdings between 04:35 and 05:15 UTC. On timeout, user-context-service executed a fallback handler that cached empty holdings ('holdings=0 sips=0') into shared cache with an excessively long TTL of 21600 seconds (6 hours). While timeout counts returned to baseline at 05:15 UTC, the poisoned cache entries caused the assistant to continue serving empty context to affected users through noon IST.

**Root cause:** During a morning timeout burst between 04:35 and 05:15 UTC, user-context-service fell back to writing an empty portfolio context ('holdings=0 sips=0') to the shared cache with a 6-hour (21600s) TTL instead of failing open or caching with a minimal transient TTL. This poisoned the cache for affected users, causing assistant-orchestrator to retrieve and present zero holdings long after upstream request timeouts returned to baseline.

## Hypotheses

Cache hit rates for the user_context keyspace rose from 93% to 98%, and user-context-service served 390 empty context reads from cache between 05:15 and 07:30 UTC, directly explaining the persistent noon symptom.

   - Supporting: [ev_4, ev_8] · Contradicting: [ev_6, ev_10, ev_21]
   - portfolio-service latency remained completely stable at 135-153ms p95 across the entire window, and timeouts in user-context-service dropped back to near-zero after 05:15 UTC without any rollback or fix to portfolio-service.

## Facts
